text: The thermostat faceplate is scratched, but its readings and temperature control work normally.
The ventilation grille paint is flaking; airflow and room temperatures are unchanged.
The bedroom air vent damper is jammed closed; the other rooms still receive conditioned air and no hazard is reported.
The AC condensate drain leaves a small contained puddle in its catch tray; cooling still works and water is not spreading.
During freezing weather the occupied apartment has no heat because the boiler stopped working.
The cooling system failed this afternoon and the occupied upstairs rooms are becoming excessively hot.
There are flames coming out of the air-handler cabinet right now.
Thick smoke is pouring from the operating furnace into the occupied hallway.
The decorative faucet cap has faded, but the tap operates normally without any leak.
The toilet seat has a surface scratch; it is secure and the toilet works normally.
The bathroom basin drains slowly, but it is usable and no water is overflowing.
A drain joint drips occasionally into a bucket; the drip is contained and the sink remains usable.
The building water supply has failed and no occupied unit has running water.
The sole water heater has stopped supplying hot water to the occupied building during cold weather.
A ruptured supply line is rapidly flooding the occupied kitchen and the water is still flowing.
Sewage is actively overflowing from the toilet and spreading across the occupied apartment.
The light switch cover has a cosmetic scratch; the switch and lights function normally.
A socket faceplate is discolored from old paint, with no heat, damage or loss of function.
One installed reading light will not turn on; the other lights work and there is no heat or smoke.
The hallway dimmer no longer adjusts brightness, but the light stays on normally with no reported hazard.
The main circuit has failed and the occupied house has no working lights or electrical outlets.
Repeated breaker trips have left the entire occupied apartment without electricity; there is no reported smoke or sparking.
The breaker cabinet is smoking and its wiring is visibly glowing red right now.
An exposed live cable is throwing sparks across the occupied entryway.
There is a small paint scuff on the bedroom wall and the wall is otherwise sound.
A kitchen cabinet handle has a cosmetic scratch; the handle and door are firmly attached and work normally.
A single window insect screen is torn; the window itself closes and locks securely.
Rainwater seeps slowly through the roof into one bucket; the leak is contained and no sagging or electrical contact is reported.
The front entrance latch has broken and the occupied property cannot be secured.
The only exterior access door is jammed shut, preventing normal use; another safe exit remains available.
Large sections of the ceiling are actively collapsing onto the occupied living-room floor.
The exterior stair landing is breaking apart while people are standing on it.
